## Example 5.7 · (a) Growth {#ss5-example-5-7-a .gp-lesson}

Consider the geometric sequences below:

a) For the GP $a_n=3\times2^{n-1}$ $(r=2>1)$:

::: {.gp-subparts}
i) Write down the equivalent continuous exponential function $f(x)$.

ii) Evaluate the first four terms and describe the shape of the plot $(n,a_n)$.
:::

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 33 · Example 5.7(a)</p>

::: notes

(i) f(x)=3×2^(x−1)=(3/2)2^x for x real. Either equivalent expression is valid. (ii) 3,6,12,24. The discrete points (1,3),(2,6),(3,12),(4,24) lie on an increasing exponential curve. Their successive increases also grow. Only the positive integer input points belong to the sequence. The graph slide's Growth preset illustrates the same values.

:::
